correctness.rationale: The morphic induction is sound. The blocks \(P_k=\mu^k(1)\) and \(Q_k=\mu^k(0)\) have length \(2^k\) and differ only in their final bit. If \(L=2^k\), every prefix from length \(L\) through \(2L-1\) is \(P_k\) followed by a prefix of a second copy of \(P_k\), so the current dyadic endpoint set remains an attractor: factors are either already represented in the first block, cross the selected boundary position, or can be shifted into the first block. At length \(2L\), the suffix \(Q_k\) occurs uniquely. Every interior length-\(L\) window is a cyclic rotation of \(P_k\), hence has the same one-count as \(P_k\), whereas \(Q_k\) differs by one bit; therefore the suffix is the only occurrence and avoids the old attractor. This forces the next greedy endpoint \(2L-1\). Independent finite replay through 128 characters and 13 dyadic levels agrees but is not used as the infinite proof.
